official.deadline_note: Immigration New Zealand states applications for the 2027 intake opened 1 July 2026 and closed 1 October 2026. No 2028 closing date is published.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake; applications open 1 July and close 1 October each year
official.status_note: The official programme page states 'Applications close: 1 October 2026', so the 2027 intake window has now closed. The next window is expected to open in July 2027, but no 2028 closing date is published.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The regulations state payment 'can be used toward tuition fees, course costs, compulsory student services fees and other living costs', but the award is a capped value of up to $25,000 rather than a guaranteed fee waiver.
benefits: A scholarship with a value set up to $25,000, paid in two equal instalments
Funds may be used toward tuition fees, course costs, compulsory student services fees and other living costs
eligibility: Be a former refugee or the child of a former refugee, where former refugees resettled through the Convention Refugee, UNHCR Quota or Community Organisation Refugee Sponsorship pathways
Have successfully completed at least one year of tertiary study
Be enrolled or intending to enrol in full-time study in a health-related qualification with at least one year of full-time study remaining at the time of the award
The qualification must be at level 7 or above and offered by an NZQA-accredited tertiary provider
Have the potential to complete your chosen qualification
Be a New Zealand Citizen, Permanent Resident or Resident visa holder and ordinarily resident in New Zealand
requirements: Must pass all first semester courses to receive second semester funding
Must supply a satisfactory report and an academic transcript at the end of each semester throughout the tenure
Must reapply each year to be considered for future funding
The scholarship may not be deferred or suspended except in exceptional circumstances with approval from the Chair of the Selection Committee
May not hold additional scholarships without the approval of the Chair of the Selection Committee
documents: Proof of permanent residency via refugee background status, most commonly an Immigration New Zealand Certificate of Identity or INZ letter confirming date of birth, refugee status and permanent residency
A CV including any prior health work experience
A statement describing your financial position, how you would use the scholarship, and the benefit it would make to you and your family
A statement on the impact you intend to have on the refugee health workforce and refugee health outcomes
A personal reference and an academic reference
Current academic transcript plus copies of any other transcripts for all previous study, including English language and foundation or preparation studies
selection_criteria: Impact of the scholar on refugee health outcomes
Impact of the scholar on the refugee health workforce
Impact of the scholarship to the scholar
Likelihood of successfully attaining the qualification
Priority is given to those studying an in-demand discipline with a short lead time until entering the workforce
coverage: Up to $25,000 per academic year, paid in two equal instalments
Usable toward tuition fees, course costs, compulsory student services fees and other living costs
application_method: Apply online through Universities New Zealand once applications have opened
Complete the application form and upload the required documents through the Community Force platform on the Universities New Zealand website
official.application_route: Apply online via the Universities New Zealand Community Force platform once the July to October window opens, uploading all statements, references and transcripts with the form.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be a New Zealand Citizen, Permanent Resident or Resident visa holder and ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
official.international_eligibility: Not an international scholarship: it is restricted to New Zealand citizens, permanent residents and resident visa holders.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The qualification must be health-related, at level 7 or above, and offered by an NZQA-accredited tertiary provider, with at least one year of full-time study remaining.
official.research_requirement: No research proposal is required; the evidence is academic transcripts, a CV, and a personal and academic reference.
official.duration: One academic year; recipients must reapply each year to be considered for future funding
official.description: The New Zealand Refugee Health Scholarship Programme was developed in 2025 by the National Leadership and Coordination Service, a partnership between MBIE / Immigration New Zealand, the Ministry of Health and Health New Zealand, to create more equitable access to health-related education and training for former refugees. Each successful applicant receives a scholarship valued up to $25,000 for one academic year.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (refugees and displaced students, health workforce)

not_confirmed: funding_amount and funding_period - the value is a capped 'up to $25,000', so the actual award per scholar is set annually by the funder and is not published

verification.notes: The value, purpose, eligibility rules, funding conditions, selection criteria, application requirements and both intake dates were read directly from Immigration New Zealand's programme page, the Universities New Zealand scholarship page, and the publicly downloadable NZ Refugee Health Scholarship Regulations dated 5 January 2026.

applicant_utility.summary: The $25,000 figure is a ceiling, not a guaranteed payment, so treat it as the maximum and check the offer letter for what you will actually receive each year. Money arrives in two equal instalments and the second one is conditional on passing every first-semester course, so a single failed paper can stop the second half of the year's funding. The programme prioritises applicants in in-demand health disciplines with a short runway to employment, so being close to finishing your qualification is a real advantage rather than a neutral factor.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Former refugees and their children living in New Zealand who have already completed at least a year of tertiary study and have at least a year left on a level 7 or above health qualification.
application_readiness_checklist: Obtain your Immigration New Zealand Certificate of Identity or INZ letter confirming date of birth, refugee status and permanent residency, since generic visa evidence is not what the regulations ask for
Gather transcripts for every prior programme including English language and foundation studies, not just your current institution's records
Secure both a personal reference and an academic reference early, since you need one of each and referees are the usual bottleneck
Write the financial statement carefully, covering how you are currently supported, how you would spend the award, and the impact on your family
Time your application so you still have at least one full-time year of study remaining at the moment of the award, not at the moment you apply
common_rejection_risks: Having less than one year of full-time study remaining when the award decision is made
Applying at a qualification below level 7 or with a provider that is not NZQA-accredited
Failing any first-semester course, which blocks the second semester instalment
Not having refugee background status documented through an INZ Certificate of Identity or INZ letter
Submitting a statement that only covers financial need without addressing workforce and health-outcome impact
Holding another scholarship without prior approval from the Chair of the Selection Committee
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any gap between the actual award and your true costs, since the $25,000 is a cap rather than a guaranteed amount, plus anything the cap does not absorb such as travel, equipment and dependants' costs.
document_audit: Refugee status must be evidenced by an INZ Certificate of Identity or INZ letter that confirms date of birth, refugee status and permanent residency all together
Transcripts are required for all previous study, including incomplete and non-degree programmes such as English language and foundation study
Two separate references are required, one personal and one academic, and they are not interchangeable
The scholarship cannot be deferred, so your enrolment plan must match the award year exactly
alerts: The application window is only three months (1 July to 1 October), and it has now closed for the 2027 intake, so plan for a July 2027 opening
Funding is annual, not for the whole degree: you must reapply each year, so winning it once is not a guarantee for the remaining years of your qualification
The committee may invite shortlisted applicants to an online interview and its decisions are final
Priority goes to in-demand disciplines with a short lead time to workforce entry, so late-stage students are favoured over early-stage ones
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: When the window reopens, complete the online form on the Universities New Zealand Community Force platform, upload the INZ status evidence, CV, statements, both references and all transcripts, and await a possible online interview for shortlisted applicants.
